note: Rules can change without notice. Always follow signboards and staff instructions on site.

visitorInstructions.photography: Not allowed inside the Ashram premises.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Modest clothing: cover shoulders and knees. No beachwear.
tips: Switch your phone off or keep it fully silent.
Keep silence, especially around the Samadhi courtyard.
Entry is free; expect a quick security check at the gate.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed on public streets and outside buildings. Ask before photographing residents or entering private courtyards.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Casual is fine on the streets. Carry a light scarf or shawl for the temples and ashram nearby.
tips: People live here: keep noise low, especially early morning and late evening.
Do not enter private gates or climb on heritage walls and balconies.
Wear comfortable shoes; pavements can be uneven and midday sun is strong.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed freely on the public promenade.
tips: Swimming is not advisable here: rocky seawall and deep water.
Do not climb on the rocks near breaking waves.
Vehicles are banned 6:00 PM to 7:30 AM, so plan to walk or cycle.
Use the bins; keep the seawall litter-free.

visitorInstructions.photography: Visitors report photography is not allowed inside. Confirm at the ticket counter.
tips: Closed on Mondays.
Keep small change ready for the entry ticket.
Do not touch the exhibits, sculptures or furniture.
Ask at the counter if large bags must be deposited.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed only from the designated viewing point. No photography inside the Matrimandir or its inner gardens.
tips: Collect your free viewing pass at the Auroville Visitors Centre first (usually after a short video).
Keep silence near the Matrimandir; do not talk in the grounds.
Inner chamber meditation needs advance booking and strict silence; no phones or large bags.
Passes can run out, so go early in the day.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually fine in the shop. Ask before photographing staff or artisan products.
tips: Opening hours are not confirmed, so check on arrival.
Handmade ceramics, textiles and leather: handle gently and ask before touching display pieces.
Browsing is free; the top-floor cafe is a good rest stop.

visitorInstructions.photography: Ask permission first. The women embroidering may not want to be photographed.
tips: Closed on Sundays.
Do not touch linen or lace that is still being worked on.
Buying directly supports the women artisans.
Keep your voice low; it is a working centre.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed. Keep phones and cameras in a dry bag during the boat ride.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Swimwear is fine on the sand. Carry a cover-up and a change of clothes.
tips: Reachable only by boat from Chunnambar Boat House. The last boat is usually around 4:30 PM, so confirm the return time.
Swim only in the marked safe zones near lifeguards; the tide can be strong.
Wear the life jacket on the boat and keep your ticket for the return.
Rough seas in monsoon (July to September) can stop boat service.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed. Ask before photographing fishermen and their families.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Beachwear is fine on the sand. Cover up when walking through the fishing village.
tips: Currents can be strong. Swim only near the shore and avoid it when waves are high.
Do not swim alone; lifeguard cover is not guaranteed.
Do not sit on or move fishing boats and nets.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed on the beach.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Beachwear is fine on the sand.
tips: This is a designated No Plastic Zone: avoid single-use plastic and take your waste with you.
Swim only in the designated area near the watchtowers.
Use the washroom facilities and bins provided.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed.
tips: Opening hours are not confirmed, so check on arrival.
Evenings and weekends get crowded around the food court; watch children and belongings.
Enter the water only if a lifeguard or sign says it is safe.
Use bins and keep the playground area clean.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Beachwear is fine on the sand. Cover up away from the beach.
tips: Swim with caution and stay close to shore; tides can be unpredictable.
Swimming is discouraged in monsoon (July to September).
Do not disturb the fishing catamarans.
Take your rubbish with you.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed from outside.
tips: This is a solemn memorial: keep voices low.
Do not climb on or lean against the monument.
It is lit up on Bastille Day (14 July).

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed; it is a popular photo spot.
tips: Do not climb the granite pillars or the statue base.
Gets busy around sunset: keep your belongings safe.
Keep the seafront clean.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed.
tips: Do not climb on or write on the heritage pavilion.
Keep off the lawns and flower beds where signs say so.
Use the bins and carry out your litter.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed outside. Ask staff whether cameras are allowed in the tower.
tips: Check the current visiting schedule before you go.
Narrow old stairs are typical: go slowly and keep a hand on the rail.
Keep small change ready for the entry ticket.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually restricted. Ask security first and never photograph guards or security installations.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Neat, formal-casual clothing; this is an official residence.
tips: Prior approval is required for a visit, so arrange it before you go.
Carry a photo ID.
If you do not have approval, enjoy the exterior view from the road.

visitorInstructions.photography: Visitors report no photos or videos inside. Ask the staff before taking any.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Modest: cover shoulders and knees. No shorts or sleeveless tops.
tips: Remove footwear before entering and use the shoe stand.
Keep your phone on silent; be ready to leave it outside if asked.
Follow the mahout's instructions near the temple elephant.

places.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus

visitorInstructions.photography: Reported to be allowed only outside. Ask before photographing inside and never use flash.
tips: It is an active place of worship: keep quiet and do not walk around during Mass.
Busiest on Sundays and during Mass times.
Do not photograph worshippers.

places.name: Église de Notre Dame des Anges

visitorInstructions.photography: Outside photos are fine. Ask before photographing inside and do not use flash.
tips: Keep silence inside; step outside to take calls.
Avoid sightseeing during services.
Do not photograph people who are praying.

places.name: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception

visitorInstructions.photography: Outside photos are fine. Ask before photographing inside and do not use flash.
tips: It is the Archdiocese's mother church and a working place of worship: be quiet.
Avoid sightseeing during Mass.
Do not photograph people who are praying.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually not allowed inside the halls and sanctum. Outside views of the gopuram are generally fine; ask staff.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Modest: cover shoulders and knees. No shorts or sleeveless tops.
tips: Remove footwear at the entrance.
Be ready to leave your phone outside if asked.
Do not touch the carved pillars or idols; follow the queue and signs.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually not allowed inside the halls and sanctum. Ask staff before using a camera.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Modest: cover shoulders and knees. No shorts or sleeveless tops.
tips: Remove footwear at the entrance.
Do not enter the sacred tank (theertham) or throw anything into it.
It is about 9 km out of town: confirm the ritual timings before you travel.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually not allowed inside. Ask staff first.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Modest: cover shoulders and knees. No shorts or sleeveless tops.
tips: Remove footwear at the entrance.
Keep your phone on silent.
Opening hours are not confirmed, so check on arrival.

visitorInstructions.photography: Ask permission before photographing inside. Never photograph people praying.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Cover arms and legs. Women should cover their hair (carry a scarf). No shorts, sleeveless or tight clothing.
tips: Remove shoes before entering the prayer area.
Avoid visiting at prayer times, especially Friday midday. Entry to the prayer hall for non-Muslims is at the caretaker's discretion, so ask politely.
Keep your phone on silent and your voice low.

visitorInstructions.photography: Ask permission before photographing inside. Never photograph people praying.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Cover arms and legs. Women should cover their hair (carry a scarf). No shorts, sleeveless or tight clothing.
tips: This is the Friday congregational mosque: avoid visiting around Friday midday prayers.
Remove shoes before entering the prayer area.
Follow the caretaker's instructions on where visitors may go.

visitorInstructions.photography: Ask permission before photographing inside. Never photograph people praying.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Cover arms and legs. Women should cover their hair (carry a scarf). No shorts, sleeveless or tight clothing.
tips: Remove shoes before entering the prayer area.
Avoid visiting during prayer times, especially Friday midday.
Keep your phone on silent and your voice low.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed in the park. Do not photograph guards or security at the nearby Raj Niwas and Assembly.
tips: Keep off the lawns and flower beds where signs say so.
Do not climb on or write on the heritage pavilion.
Use the bins and carry out your litter.

visitorInstructions.photography: Personal photos are fine. Professional shoots (photo-shoots, short films) need a permit and a fee set by the Puducherry government.
tips: Do not pluck flowers or plants or walk on the garden beds.
Keep to the walkways.
Children below a set age get free entry; check the ticket counter.

visitorInstructions.photography: Ask at the counter; small museums often restrict cameras.
tips: Closed on Mondays and public holidays.
Do not touch the dolls and puppets.
Keep children close to the display cases.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed. Keep gadgets in a dry bag on the boats.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Casual clothing and sandals or sports shoes you do not mind getting wet.
tips: The last boat to Paradise Beach is usually around 4:30 PM, so arrive early.
Wear the life jacket and follow the crew's instructions.
A parking fee applies; confirm current ticket prices at the counter.

visitorInstructions.photography: Welcome. Use a long lens for birds, no flash, and do not approach nests.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Muted, earthy colours, a hat and long sleeves for sun and insects.
tips: Move slowly and stay quiet near the water; noise and horns scare the birds.
The lake is meant to be plastic-free: carry a reusable bottle and take all litter out.
Bring binoculars. Mornings and the migratory season (roughly November to February) are best.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed at the open site. Ask the caretaker if any area is restricted.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Light, covered clothing, a hat and sturdy shoes.
tips: It is a protected archaeological site: do not dig or collect beads and pottery pieces.
Do not climb on old structures.
Shade is limited near the riverbank, so carry water.

visitorInstructions.photography: Fine inside the Centre. Photography is restricted around the Matrimandir.
tips: Collect your free Matrimandir viewing pass here (usually after a short video).
Auroville is a living community, not a theme park: respect its quiet and privacy.
The information desk closes in the afternoon, so arrive well before 5 PM.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed; popular photo spot on the promenade.
tips: Do not climb the statue or its base.
Busy around sunset: keep your belongings safe.
Keep the seafront clean.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed; popular photo spot on the promenade.
tips: Do not climb the statue or its base.
Busy around sunset: keep your belongings safe.
Keep the seafront clean.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually restricted in the reading rooms. Ask staff before photographing books or manuscripts.
tips: Keep silence and put your phone on silent.
Rare manuscripts are for reference only: ask the librarian before handling anything.
Closed on Mondays and public holidays.

visitorInstructions.photography: Usually restricted in the archives and library. Ask first.
tips: This is a working research institute: visit only in weekday hours and ask at reception before going in.
Do not touch the archives or manuscripts.
Keep your voice low.

visitorInstructions.photography: Fine in public areas. Ask staff during events and screenings.
tips: Check the event schedule for screenings, salons and talks.
Keep your phone silent during events.
Hours listed are office hours, so confirm before you go.

visitorInstructions.photography: Exterior photos are fine. Do not photograph security staff, and ask before going inside.
tips: It is a working municipal office: enter only with permission.
Exterior viewing only unless access is permitted.
Opening details are not confirmed, so check on arrival.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed. Ask fishermen and workers before photographing them.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Casual clothing and shoes with a good grip.
tips: The pier and ruins can be slippery or uneven: watch your step, especially after rain.
Do not sit or stand on broken edges.
Take your litter with you.

visitorInstructions.photography: Ask before photographing residents and workers. Some farms are private working sites.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Light, covered clothing and closed shoes.
tips: Opening details are not confirmed: check with the Visitors Centre first.
Enter only places that welcome visitors.
Do not pick crops or disturb the seed banks and plots.

visitorInstructions.photography: Allowed.
visitorInstructions.dressCode: Casual clothing; cover up away from the beach.
tips: It is about 130 km from central Pondicherry: plan it as a full day trip.
Currents can be strong where the river meets the sea. Swim only if locals or lifeguards say it is safe.
Opening details are not confirmed, so check on arrival.
